title: Mughal Bengal, Baro-Bhuyans, and Frontier Politics
tagline: Imperial incorporation, riverine resistance, and subah administration
intro: Follow Mughal Bengal through Rajmahal, Baro-Bhuyan resistance, Dhaka’s rise, Chittagong, and Shaista Khan’s long governorship.
description: Explore Mughal Bengal through imperial expansion, regional rulers, Bhati resistance, Dhaka-Jahangirnagar, riverine warfare, and local power struggles.
seoTitle: Mughal Bengal, Baro-Bhuyans, Isa Khan, Dhaka and Shaista Khan
seoDescription: Study Mughal Bengal through the Battle of Rajmahal, Baro-Bhuyan resistance, Isa Khan, Dhaka, Chittagong, Shaista Khan, sources, and figures.
beginnerSummary: Begin with Rajmahal and the Baro-Bhuyans to see how Bengal moved from Afghan-Karrani power into Mughal provincial rule.
advancedSummary: Compare imperial chronicles with regional resistance, river geography, revenue integration, and the administrative growth of Dhaka.

faq.question: Why are the Baro-Bhuyans central?
faq.answer: They show that Mughal incorporation was contested locally and shaped by Bengal’s riverine geography and regional elites.

faq.question: Why does Dhaka matter in this topic?
faq.answer: Dhaka’s rise as Jahangirnagar marks a major administrative and military center for Mughal consolidation in eastern Bengal.

faq.question: How should I use the sources?
faq.answer: Read imperial chronicle-based sources alongside regional reference entries on Isa Khan, Shaista Khan, Dhaka, and Chittagong.
